text:
people_ops_anna: Thanks everyone for coming to today's all-hands! We ran out of time on the pricing Q&A, so drop follow-ups about pricing/packaging/credits/rate-limits here and leadership will answer live over the next hour.

sam_sre: Quick one — are rate limits enforced per API key, per project, or per org? Trying to understand our internal test rigs that share keys.

cto_jen: Short answer: by default limits are scoped to projects (the project key). For enterprise accounts we can apply org-level quotas on top of that.

cto_jen: Practically, if you share a single project key across many services you will hit the project quota. Best practice: create per-service projects or use the org quota feature for centralized limits.

dev_ben: Is there a CLI to check current quota/usage? Wanted to script alerts for our test cluster.

ops_lee: You can query via Console -> Usage, or use the API. Example curl to get current usage for a project:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage/projects/PROJECT_ID
```

finance_john: On credits: trial credits granted at sign-up expire after 90 days from issuance. Promo credits are labeled in the Console; expiration depends on the promo. We try to call these out in the billing email.

sam_sre: If a customer hits quota, is there automatic degradation (like a soft-fallback to smaller model) or hard 429s?

cto_jen: Default behavior is a 429 when you exceed rate limits. For hosted routes we offer routing policies that can failover to a lower-cost/compatible model variant if configured (this is opt-in). We don't silently downgrade without the route policy.

product_maya: Related packaging note: we're consolidating two small tiers into a single "Developer" SKU to simplify billing. That will affect token allotments and rate limits for new signups next quarter; existing customers will be grandfathered for at least 6 months.

dev_ben: Will usage-based billing still have burst allowances or are limits strictly enforced?

cto_jen: We support burst capacity via short-term burst credits for most hosted accounts (subject to abuse detection). For Dedicated there are configurable burst windows in the contract. If you need higher sustained capacity, request a Dedicated seat or raise rate limits via the Console.

ops_lee: How do teams request quota increases?

cto_jen: Console -> Support -> Request quota increase is the fastest. For enterprise/Dedicated customers open a support ticket or contact your account rep; for public tier we do automated checks and often approve within 24–48 hours.

finance_john: Refunds on unused credits are not issued except in special enterprise contract cases. We provide credit transfers (internal promo credit issuance) on a case-by-case basis — contact billing.

sam_sre: Are there any new guardrails for abuse detection we should know about (we hit a rate-limiting spike last month)?

support_bot: [incident-bot] Noted — there was a transient spike 2025-09-14 15:23 UTC, downstream mitigation temporarily increased strictness. Ops/infra are following up in #eng-infra.

product_maya: Follow-up: we'll publish a short FAQ + examples (how to structure projects, when to use org quotas, CLI snippets) early next week and pin in the Console and docs.

people_ops_anna: Thanks all — I'll keep this thread open for another hour for any late Qs, and we'll add the FAQ link once it's live. :thumbsup:
